q: Which type of banking operates through a network of branches and is the most common banking system?
explain: Branch banking uses a branch network, the face of the bank where customers meet officials; it is the most common type.

q: Unit banking, where a bank works from a single branch for the local community, originated in:
explain: Unit banking originated in the USA and focuses on the local community, usually from one office or a few branches in one area.

q: When a bank undertakes commercial banking and investment banking activities together, it is called:
explain: Mixed banking combines commercial and investment banking under one bank.

q: When a group of persons owns and controls three or more independently chartered banks, the system is called:
explain: Chain banking means common ownership and control of three or more separately chartered banks.

q: Which type of banking involves understanding a customer's needs before offering a special product or service?
explain: Relationship banking goes beyond the normal services and relies on knowing existing and potential clients.

q: Under which system do big banks offer commercial banking, investment banking, mutual funds, merchant banking and insurance together?
explain: Universal banking provides a wide variety of financial services under one roof. Mixed banking is only commercial plus investment.

q: Which committee is best known in India for giving the concept of narrow banking as a solution to the NPA problem?
explain: The Tarapore Committee is associated with narrow banking in the context of NPAs.

q: Narrow banking is best described as:
options: The antonym of universal banking, narrow in the engagement of funds
explain: Narrow banking is the opposite of universal banking; it is narrow in how funds are engaged, not about the number of branches.

q: The type of banking aimed at giving the poor easy formal credit, minimum account-opening requirements and friendly staff is:
explain: Social banking focuses on the development needs of the poor with easy access and credit.

q: A bank with no branch network that offers services through online and telephone banking is known as:
explain: Virtual banking, also called direct banking, works remotely through online, telephone and agent networks, with ATM access possible.

q: Which statement about unit banking is correct?
options: The bank owns three independently chartered banks
The bank offers insurance and mutual funds
The bank has no physical presence at all
The bank works from a single branch or a few branches in the same area
explain: Unit banking serves a local community, often from one office; the other options describe chain, universal and virtual banking.

q: Rural banking has become integral to Indian financial markets mainly because:
options: Rural banks earn the highest profit
A majority of Indians live in rural or semi-urban areas
Urban banking is not allowed by law
Rural banks are all foreign owned
explain: A majority of the Indian population still lives in rural or semi-urban areas, so rural banking is vital.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three broad categories of the organised banking system in India?
explain: The organised system is the RBI, commercial banks and co-operative banks.

q: The RBI is called the Reserve Bank because it:
options: Keeps the cash reserves of all scheduled banks
Insures all deposits up to a limit
explain: RBI holds the cash reserves of scheduled banks, hence the name.

q: A bank is a scheduled bank when it is included in:
options: The First Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934
The Second Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934
The Second Schedule of the Constitution
The Second Schedule of the Banking Regulation Act
explain: Scheduled status comes from inclusion in the Second Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934, along with RBI-prescribed capital and reserves.

q: Non-scheduled banks are those commercial banks that:
options: Are owned only by foreign companies
Are not regulated by any law
Are included in the First Schedule of the RBI Act
Are not included in the Second Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934
explain: Non-scheduled banks are simply the ones outside the Second Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934.

q: Which of the following is NOT part of the scheduled banking structure in India?
explain: Scheduled banks include commercial banks (public, private, RRBs) and some co-operative banks. Money lenders are not part of it.

q: Which institution is the supreme monetary and banking authority of India?
explain: RBI controls the banking system and is the monetary authority.

q: Which of the following banking activities is NOT a feature of a commercial bank?
explain: Currency issue is a central bank function; commercial banks take deposits, lend and sell financial products.

q: Which of the following banks is generally NOT considered a commercial bank?
options: A foreign bank operating in India
explain: Development banks give long-term project finance rather than ordinary commercial banking.

q: Public sector banks account for roughly what share of the banking business in India, as per the book?
explain: The book says public sector banks account for over 80% of banking business and dominate commercial banking.

q: Which is the largest commercial bank of India in terms of volume?
explain: SBI is the largest commercial bank in terms of volume among all commercial banks.

q: Foreign banks in India can operate through:
explain: Foreign banks have their head offices abroad and operate in India via branches or wholly-owned subsidiaries.

q: Which of the following is an example of a foreign bank in India?
explain: HSBC, Citi Bank and Standard Chartered are foreign banks operating in India.

q: Private sector banks are those whose equity is held by:
explain: Private sector banks have equity held by private shareholders; ICICI and HDFC are examples.

q: Which bank announced on 30 March 2022 that it would acquire Citigroup's consumer business in India for about $1.6 billion?
explain: Axis Bank announced the deal worth about ₹12,325 crore.

q: YONO (You Only Need One) app was launched by which bank?
explain: YONO is SBI's digital banking platform.

q: Which of the following is the correct pair of bank and year of establishment, as per the book?
explain: Federal Bank 1931 (Kochi). DCB is 1930, City Union 1904 and J and K 1938.

q: Which of these banks is the oldest, as per the list in the book?
explain: City Union Bank (1904) is the oldest in the list; Karur Vysya was 1916, Federal 1931 and RBL 1943.

q: Dhanlaxmi Bank has its headquarters in:
explain: Dhanlaxmi Bank (1927) is headquartered in Thrissur; Federal Bank is in Kochi.

q: Which bank is headquartered in Srinagar?
explain: J and K Bank, established in 1938, is headquartered in Srinagar.

q: Which of the following banks has its headquarters in Kolkata?
explain: Bandhan Bank (2015) is headquartered in Kolkata. IDFC First, IndusInd and Yes are in Mumbai.

q: Which three banks in the book's table were all established in 1994?
options: Axis Bank, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank
IDBI Bank, Axis Bank and Yes Bank
HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and IndusInd Bank
Kotak Mahindra Bank, Yes Bank and Bandhan Bank
explain: HDFC, ICICI and IndusInd were all set up in 1994. Axis is 1993.

q: Which two banks were established in 2015?
options: Bandhan Bank and IDFC First Bank
Kotak Mahindra Bank and Yes Bank
explain: Bandhan Bank and IDFC First Bank were both set up in 2015; Kotak (2003) and Yes (2004) are earlier.

q: Kotak Mahindra Bank was established in which year, per the book?
explain: Kotak Mahindra Bank dates from 2003 and Yes Bank from 2004.

q: Which bank was established in 1964 and is headquartered in Mumbai, as per the table?
explain: IDBI Bank is listed as established in 1964.

q: Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) mainly provide credit to:
options: Small and marginal farmers, agricultural labourers and artisans
explain: RRBs are aimed at developing the rural economy and lend to small farmers, labourers and artisans.

q: Which committee's recommendations led to the setting up of Regional Rural Banks?
explain: The government set up the Narasimham Working Group in 1975; its report led to the RRB Ordinance and the 1976 Act.

q: The Regional Rural Banks Act was passed in which year?
explain: The Ordinance of September 1975 was replaced by the RRB Act, 1976.

q: The first Regional Rural Bank, set up on 2 October 1975, was:
explain: Prathama Grameen Bank, sponsored by Syndicate Bank, started with its head office at Moradabad.

q: The first RRB, Prathama Grameen Bank, was sponsored by which bank?
explain: Syndicate Bank sponsored Prathama Grameen Bank, with its head office at Moradabad.

q: What is the ownership pattern of an RRB (Centre : sponsor bank : State)?
explain: Central Government holds 50%, the sponsor bank 35% and the State Government 15%.

q: Which institution holds the apex position in agricultural and rural development, including refinance for RRBs?
explain: NABARD is the apex institution for agriculture and rural development.

q: Which of the following is NOT a function of NABARD?
options: Providing direct loans to individual agricultural farmers
Promotion and development of rural credit
Monitoring and supervision of rural credit institutions
explain: NABARD refinances co-operative banks and RRBs and does development and supervision work, but does not lend directly to individual farmers.

q: Which of the following Union Territories has Regional Rural Banks, as per the book's explanation?
options: Puducherry, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh
Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh
explain: RRBs work across 26 states and 3 UTs: Puducherry, Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh.

q: The Regional Rural Banks (Amendment) Act, 2015 raised the authorised capital of RRBs to:
explain: The Act raised authorised capital to ₹2,000 crore, not to be reduced below ₹1 crore.

q: Under the 2015 Amendment, the combined shareholding of the Centre and the sponsor bank in an RRB must be fixed at:
explain: The combined holding of the Centre and the sponsor bank is fixed at up to 51%.

q: What is the tenure of a director of an RRB after the 2015 amendment?
explain: The amendment raised director tenure to 3 years, at the pleasure of the central government.

q: Which statement about RRB directors under the 2015 Act is correct?
options: A director may hold seats on any number of RRB boards
A director of one RRB cannot be on the board of another RRB
explain: The Act bars a director of one RRB from being on the board of another.

q: In March 2020 the Union government approved a recapitalisation plan for RRBs of about:
explain: The ₹1,340 crore plan aimed at improving the RRBs' CRAR; the central share was linked to the sponsor bank releasing its share.

q: The 2020 RRB recapitalisation plan was meant to improve which ratio?
explain: The recapitalisation was meant to strengthen CRAR.

q: Co-operative banks are organised under which Act, as per the book?
explain: Co-operative banks are organised under the Co-operative Credit Societies Act, 1912 of the states.

q: The major beneficiary of co-operative banking is:
explain: Co-operative banking mainly benefits agriculture and, in general, the rural sector.

q: Which is the apex level of the three-tier short and medium-term co-operative credit structure?
explain: State co-operative banks are at the apex, central co-operative banks at district level and primary societies at the base.

q: Central co-operative banks (CCBs) operate at which level?
explain: CCBs work at district level between the state apex banks and primary societies.

q: Primary Credit Societies are formed at the:
explain: PCS operate in one locality, with borrowing and non-borrowing members decided locally.

q: The cooperative credit institutions in India are mainly of which two kinds?
explain: Agricultural co-operatives are dominant; there are also non-agricultural ones.

q: Which of the following is NOT required to open a bank account?
explain: Opening an account needs KYC documents such as identity and address proof and photographs, not a domicile certificate.

q: What is the full form of BCSBI?
options: Banking Credit and Standards Board of India
Banking Codes and Service Board of India
Banking Credit and Service Board of India
Banking Codes and Standards Board of India
explain: BCSBI stands for Banking Codes and Standards Board of India, set up for voluntary registration of banks.
